title: Investigate automated test for AGENTS.md no-fallback rule
description:
AGENTS.md says 'never add graceful fallbacks, silent defaults, or backwards-compatibility shims.' This is currently enforced only by code review. A grep-based test could catch patterns like bare excepts, broad Exception catches, `.get(x, None)`, `or []`, and silent None returns.

The concern is the allowlist would be massive — many legitimate uses of these patterns exist. Investigate whether it's feasible to write a test with a manageable allowlist, or whether the false-positive rate makes it impractical.

Inspired by jmduke.com/posts/weird-tests-2.html ('regressions for things I feel silly flagging in code review').
